flawed_step: Triangle-freeness does not imply 4-colourability; iterated Mycielski construction preserves triangle-freeness while increasing chromatic number.
counterexample: Let C5 have vertices 1,...,5 and cycle edges 12,23,34,45,51. For any graph G with vertices v1,...,vn, define M(G) on vertices v1,...,vn,u1,...,un,w: retain every edge vi-vj of G, add ui-vj and uj-vi for every edge vi-vj of G, and add w-ui for every i. Take H=M(M(C5)), an explicit graph with 23 vertices. M(G) is triangle-free whenever G is: a triangle containing w would require adjacent u-vertices, none of which exist; a triangle not containing w would either lie in G or, if it contains ui, correspond to a triangle through vi in G. Also χ(M(G))=χ(G)+1. Indeed, the upper bound follows by colouring vi and ui like vi and giving w a new colour. Conversely, from any k-colouring of M(G), rename w's colour k and recolour each vi having colour k with the colour of ui; this gives a (k−1)-colouring of G. Since χ(C5)=3, χ(H)=5. Thus H is finite, simple, triangle-free, and not 4-colourable.
assessment_summary: The twice-iterated Mycielski graph of the 5-cycle is a checked concrete counterexample: it is triangle-free and has chromatic number 5.
